question: How much money was allotted by the Gujarat government in August 2023 for the One District, One Product (ODOP) Programme to promote its indigenous products at the international level?
solution:
The correct answer is __**₹58 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In August 2023, the Gujarat government allocated **₹58 crores** for the **One District, One Product (ODOP)** programme to promote indigenous products at the international level.
 
• The ODOP initiative aims to identify and promote unique products from each district, enhancing their market reach and economic potential.
 
• Under this scheme, more than 25 handicraft products from 21 districts, including traditional crafts like **Gamthi Block Print** and **Mata-ni-Pachedi**, have been selected for promotion.
 
• The Gujarat State Handicrafts and Handloom Development Corporation (GSHHDC) is responsible for implementing the ODOP scheme in the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **One District, One Product (ODOP):** A government initiative aimed at fostering balanced regional development by identifying and promoting unique products from each district.
 
• **Gujarat State Handicrafts and Handloom Development Corporation (GSHHDC):** An organization dedicated to the development and promotion of handicrafts and handlooms in Gujarat.
 
• **Gamthi Block Print:** A traditional hand-block printing technique from Gujarat, known for its intricate designs and vibrant colors.
 
• **Mata-ni-Pachedi:** A traditional art form from Gujarat involving hand-painted or block-printed cloth used as a backdrop in temples.
 
• **International Promotion:** The ODOP scheme includes strategies to enhance the global visibility and marketability of selected products through branding, exhibitions, and e-commerce platforms.
 
• **Economic Empowerment:** By promoting district-specific products, the ODOP initiative aims to boost local economies, create employment opportunities, and preserve traditional crafts.
